title: Assistant settings — round 4: the real folder picker, and two popups

steps.headline: Default project folder — the row renamed, and the picker replaced.
steps.changed: Two things from your notes. The row is called Default project folder now, matching Default model above it. And the control is no longer a look-alike: it is the same folder picker the new conversation form uses, folder icon and all.
steps.notice: The picker shows the folder's short name — youcoded — with the folder icon beside it, exactly as it does when you start a conversation.
steps.risk: None here; the next step opens it.

steps.path: Settings → Assistant settings → General → the folder picker, open
steps.headline: Open, it is the same list, with the same rows and the same last line.
steps.changed: Your saved folders with their names, paths and sync dots, a tick on the one in use, and Browse for folder… at the bottom for anything not on the list.
steps.notice: This is the same picker used in two places, not a copy of it — so it cannot drift away from the new conversation form later.
steps.risk: Someone with no saved folders sees a list with only Browse for folder… in it. That is the same thing they see on the new conversation form today.

steps.path: Settings → Assistant settings → Permissions → turning the switch on
steps.headline: The red banner is gone. Turning the switch on now stops you and makes you tick a box.
steps.changed: Flipping the switch opens this and the switch does not move until you press Turn it on — which stays greyed out until the box is ticked. Turning it back off is instant; only the dangerous direction is gated.
steps.notice: What the popup says is measured behaviour, not a guess: we tested Claude Code with this flag on, and the only thing it still refused was a command that would delete the whole project folder.
steps.risk: It is a longer read than the banner it replaces, every single time you turn it on.

steps.path: Settings → Assistant settings → Cloud providers → Sign out
steps.headline: Sign out on Claude Code tells you where to do it, and signs nothing out.
steps.changed: Your call from the last round. The button stays on the card so it matches ChatGPT's, and pressing it explains that Claude Code holds its own sign-in and points at the one place that clears it.
steps.notice: The app already says this same thing anywhere Claude Code's own commands are listed, so the two agree.
steps.risk: It hands the reader a typed command in a terminal, which is the one thing this app tries never to do. If that bothers you, the honest alternative is dropping the button.
